verses: As for man, his days are like grass—he blooms like a flower of the field;
when the wind passes over, it vanishes, and its place remembers it no more.
But from everlasting to everlasting the loving devotion of the LORD extends to those who fear Him, and His righteousness to their children’s children—
to those who keep His covenant and remember to obey His precepts.
The LORD has established His throne in heaven, and His kingdom rules over all.
Bless the LORD, all His angels mighty in strength who carry out His word, who hearken to the voice of His command.
Bless the LORD, all His hosts, you servants who do His will.
Bless the LORD, all His works in all places of His dominion. Bless the LORD, O my soul!
title: Love That Outlasts Us
season_line: It's Veterans Day, a day for remembering people who gave years of their lives for others, two weeks before we gather to give thanks.
big_idea: Our lives are short, but God's love isn't, and that changes what's worth living for.
frame: Most of what fills a Wednesday will be forgotten by Friday: the emails, the errands, the small worries. On Veterans Day we feel the opposite pull, the wish to honor lives that gave something lasting. Scripture is honest that we are passing, but it doesn't leave us there. What lasts is God's faithful love, and it reaches through us to the people who come after us. So the question for today isn't how to be remembered, but how to pass on what we've been given.

carry.text: But from everlasting to everlasting the loving devotion of the LORD extends to those who fear Him, and His righteousness to their children’s children—

glance.head: Life is short
glance.line: We bloom like a wildflower, and when the wind passes over, we're gone.

glance.head: His love is not
glance.line: God's loving devotion lasts forever and carries on to our children's children.

glance.head: He reigns over all
glance.line: His throne is in heaven, and His kingdom rules over everything.

glance.head: Everything bless Him
glance.line: Angels, heaven's armies, all creation, and finally David's own soul are called to praise.

understand: Verses 15–16 use a picture Israel knew well: wildflowers that cover the hills in spring and are gone after one hot, dry wind. Isaiah uses the same image, and Peter quotes him ({{Isaiah 40:6-8|Isaiah 40:6–8}}, {{1 Peter 1:24-25|1 Peter 1:24–25}}). The point isn't gloom. It's honesty: our lives are brief.

Then comes the turn in verse 17, with one small word: *But*. Our days are short, but God's love is everlasting, and it doesn't stop with us. It reaches our children's children. Verse 18 says who it rests on: people who keep His covenant and remember to obey. Remembering is the thread that runs through this whole psalm.

Jesus used the same picture. He pointed to the wildflowers and the grass of the field, here today and gone tomorrow, to show how carefully the Father cares even for passing things, and how much more He cares for us ({{Matthew 6:28-30|Matthew 6:28–30}}).

The psalm ends by widening the circle. Angels, the armies of heaven, and every created thing everywhere are called to bless the Lord. Then David brings it back home to the one voice he's responsible for, his own. The last line is the same as the first.

word.gloss: Covenant love that keeps its promises. Yesterday it crowned us; today we learn how long it lasts: from everlasting to everlasting.

glow: Bless the LORD, O my soul!

god.short: Thank God for one person whose faith reached you.
god.full: Read verse 17 slowly. Thank God by name for one person whose faith reached you, and pray for one person your faith might reach.
god.why: His love runs on to children's children ({{Psalm 103:17|Psalm 103:17}}).

together.short: Each name one person whose faith shaped yours.
together.full: Over coffee or on the way out the door, each of you name one person whose faith shaped yours.

others.short: Thank a veteran you know, by name, today.
others.full: It's Veterans Day. Send a veteran you know a short note thanking them for something specific, and tell them you're praying for them.
others.why: Honoring people who are owed honor is part of loving them ({{Romans 13:7|Romans 13:7}}).

tonight: What do we hope people remember about our faith long after we're gone?
